assignedReviews.card_evidence: Punctuated equilibrium is an evolutionary pattern
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes punctuated equilibrium, an evolutionary biology concept, which has no connection to observing celestial objects in the sky. The assigned competency G3-E-6 concerns the Sun, Moon, planets, and stars, so the tag is unrelated and at the wrong grade/domain.

copy.en: Punctuated equilibrium is an evolutionary pattern where species stay mostly unchanged for long periods, then undergo rapid change in short bursts.
copy.tl: Ang punctuated equilibrium ay isang pattern ng evolution kung saan ang mga species ay halos hindi nagbabago sa mahabang panahon, pagkatapos ay mabilis na nagbabago sa maikling panahon.
copy.bis: Ang punctuated equilibrium usa ka pattern sa evolution diin ang mga species halos dili mausab sa taas nga panahon, dayon paspas nga mausab sa mubo nga panahon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The human reproductive system is a group of organs that works together to produce new individuals through reproduction.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and explain evidence that current continents are separate parts of what was a single continent millions of years ago
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the purpose of the human reproductive system, which is unrelated to the competency about evidence for continental drift and a single ancient continent.

copy.en: The human reproductive system is a group of organs that works together to produce new individuals through reproduction.
copy.tl: Ang human reproductive system ay grupo ng mga organ na nagtutulungan upang makabuo ng bagong indibidwal sa pamamagitan ng reproduction.
copy.bis: Ang human reproductive system usa ka grupo sa mga organ nga magtinabangay aron makahimo og bag-ong indibidwal pinaagi sa reproduction.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A force is simply a push or a pull that you apply to an object
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain what volcanoes are and how they are formed
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines force as a push or pull; it contains no information about volcanoes or how they are formed.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A force is simply a push or a pull that you apply to an object
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the difference between heat and temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about force as push/pull, not about the difference between heat and temperature.

copy.en: The push and pull of a magnet is called magnetic force.
copy.tl: Ang pagtulak at paghila ng magnet ay tinatawag na magnetic force.
copy.bis: Ang pagtulod ug pagbira sa magnet gitawag ug magnetic force.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Magnetic force is the push or pull that a magnet exerts on certain objects.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how light and sound can be harmful to people and make suggestions on how to protect oneself from them
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines magnetic force, which is unrelated to the competency about explaining how light and sound can be harmful and suggesting protection measures.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Magnetic force is the push or pull that a magnet exerts on certain objects.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: research using secondary sources to identify how the properties of waves are described using scientific terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, and velocity
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes magnetic force, not wave properties described with terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, and velocity.

copy.en: Magnetic force is the push or pull that a magnet exerts on certain objects.
copy.tl: Ang magnetic force ay ang pagtulak o paghila na ginagawa ng magnet sa ilang mga bagay.
copy.bis: Ang magnetic force mao ang pagtulod o pagbira nga gihimo sa magnet sa pipila ka mga butang.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: concentration must be expressed quantitatively using numbers, such as percent by mass or percent by volume
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the difference between heat and temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses quantitative expression of concentration (percent by mass/volume) in laboratory work, which is a chemistry/solutions topic. G7-F-8 requires explaining the difference between heat and temperature, a physics/heat concept. There is no overlap in content or skill.

copy.en: For laboratory work, concentration must be expressed quantitatively using numbers, such as percent by mass or percent by volume, to be exact.
copy.tl: Para sa laboratory work, kailangang ipahayag ang concentration nang quantitative gamit ang mga numero, tulad ng percent by mass o percent by volume, para maging eksakto.
copy.bis: Alang sa laboratory work, kinahanglan ipahayag ang concentration sa quantitative nga paagi gamit ang mga numero, sama sa percent by mass o percent by volume, aron mahimong eksakto.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A quasar is the super bright core of a faraway galaxy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about the general structure of the solar system and its major celestial objects (planets, etc.). A quasar is an extragalactic object, not part of the solar system, and the card provides no information about solar system structure or its components.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A quasar is the super bright core of a faraway galaxy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The competency concerns natural objects commonly seen in the sky (Sun, Moon, planets, stars). Quasars are not commonly seen, are not among the listed objects, and the card does not support observing or describing those sky objects.

copy.en:
What is a quasar?

A quasar is the super bright core of a faraway galaxy where a supermassive black hole gobbles up matter, releasing more light than the rest of the galaxy — billions of times brighter than our Sun!
copy.tl:
Ano ang quasar?

Ang quasar ay ang napakaliwanag na core ng malayong galaxy kung saan ang supermassive black hole ay lumalamon ng matter, naglalabas ng mas maraming liwanag kaysa sa buong galaxy — bilyun-bilyong beses na mas maliwanag kaysa sa Araw!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang quasar?

Ang quasar mao ang grabe ka hayag nga core sa layo nga galaxy diin ang supermassive black hole naglamoy og daghang matter, nagpagawas og suga nga labing hayag kaysa sa tibuok galaxy — bilyun-bilyon ka beses nga mas hayag kaysa sa Adlaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Keep a towel that can absorb water well and dry quickly
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes physical properties (absorbency and drying speed) of a towel, not chemical properties such as being burnt, reacting with other materials, or being degradable/biodegradable as required by G4-M-3.

copy.en: Keep a towel that can absorb water well and dry quickly so you can use it again after getting wet in the rain.
copy.tl: Magtabi ng tuwalya na mahusay sumipsip ng tubig at mabilis matuyo para magamit muli pagkatapos mabasa sa ulan.
copy.bis: Pagtipig ug tualya nga maayo mosuyop ug tubig ug dali nga mauga aron magamit pag-usab pagkahuman mabasa sa ulan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Radar is used to track weather disturbances, guide airplanes, and even catch traffic violators
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: Radar uses are not how an interaction brings good or harm.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Radar is used to track weather disturbances, guide airplanes, and even catch traffic violators
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe that living things interact with each other in the natural environment, such as through competition, or predation
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not living things interacting through competition or predation.

copy.en: Radar is used to track weather disturbances, guide airplanes, and even catch traffic violators by measuring how fast their vehicles are moving.
copy.tl: Ginagamit ang radar para subaybayan ang mga weather disturbance, gabayan ang mga eroplano, at hulihin pa nga ang mga traffic violator sa pamamagitan ng pagsukat kung gaano kabilis ang takbo ng kanilang mga sasakyan.
copy.bis: Ang radar gigamit sa pagsubay sa mga weather disturbance, paggiya sa mga eroplano, ug pagdakop pa gani sa mga traffic violator pinaagi sa pagsukod kung unsa kapaspas ang dagan sa ilang mga sakyanan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A radio changes electrical energy into sound energy so we can hear music, and it also produces heat energy while it is playing.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe using labeled diagrams the biotic and abiotic features of tropical rainforests, swamps, estuaries, mangrove forests, and coral reefs
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about energy conversion in a radio (electrical to sound and heat). G9-L-9 requires describing biotic and abiotic features of specific ecosystems using labeled diagrams. There is no connection to ecosystems, biodiversity, or labeled diagrams.

copy.en: A radio changes electrical energy into sound energy so we can hear music, and it also produces heat energy while it is playing.
copy.tl: Ang radyo ay nagpapalit ng electrical energy para maging sound energy upang makarinig tayo ng musika, at gumagawa rin ito ng heat energy habang tumutugtog.
copy.bis: Ang radyo nag-ilis sa electrical energy aron mahimong sound energy aron makadungog kita og musika, ug naghimo usab kini og heat energy samtang nagpatukar.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A rainy day has falling rain, cloudy sky, and often cooler temperature than a sunny day.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes weather conditions of a rainy day, which is unrelated to the respiratory system (nose, windpipe, lungs) or any living-things content. The assigned competency is entirely mismatched.

copy.en: A rainy day has falling rain, cloudy sky, and often cooler temperature than a sunny day.
copy.tl: Ang maulan na araw ay may bumabagsak na ulan, maulap na kalangitan, at kadalasang mas malamig na temperature kaysa maaraw na araw.
copy.bis: Ang rainy day adunay nagbunok nga ulan, dag-om nga kalangitan, ug sagad mas bugnaw nga temperature kaysa sunny day.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You draw at least two refracted rays, and the place where they intersect is the tip of the image!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate proper handling and disposal of materials according to their properties, such as reusing objects, disposing of excess oil into garbage, and recycling paper, plastic or glass
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches how to locate an image formed by a lens using ray diagrams (intersection of refracted rays). G3-M-7 is about proper handling and disposal of materials according to their properties (reusing, recycling, disposing of oil). There is no connection to materials handling or disposal; the topic is optics, not matter handling.

copy.en:
How do you find the image made by a lens using ray diagrams?

You draw at least two refracted rays, and the place where they intersect is the tip of the image!
copy.tl:
Paano mo mahahanap ang imahe na gawa ng lens gamit ang ray diagrams?

Gumuhit ka ng hindi bababa sa dalawang refracted rays, at ang lugar kung saan sila nag-intersect ay ang dulo ng imahe!
copy.bis:
Unsaon nimo pagpangita ang imahe nga gihimo sa lens gamit ang ray diagrams?

Magdrowing ka og labing menos duha ka refracted rays, ug ang lugar diin sila mag-intersect mao ang tumoy sa imahe!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Reading food labels helps you know what ingredients and additives are inside the food before you eat it.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate and explain the observable effects of predictable patterns and events including changes in seasons, changes observed in the patterns of visible star over a year, and solar and lunar eclipses
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about reading food labels and identifying ingredients/additives, which has no connection to the Sun-Earth-Moon system, seasons, star patterns, or eclipses described in G6-E-8.

copy.en: Reading food labels helps you know what ingredients and additives are inside the food before you eat it.
copy.tl: Ang pagbabasa ng food label ay nakakatulong para malaman mo kung anong mga sangkap at additives ang nasa loob ng pagkain bago mo ito kainin.
copy.bis: Ang pagbasa sa food label makatabang aron mahibalo ka kon unsa nga mga sangkap ug additives ang anaa sa sulod sa pagkaon sa dili pa nimo kini kaonon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Laboratory safety follows three simple phases
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes laboratory safety phases (READY, CAREFUL, CLEAN), which is unrelated to observing the outer parts of plants and identifying their roles in obtaining water and nutrients. No instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: Laboratory safety follows three simple phases: be READY before an experiment, be CAREFUL during it, and CLEAN up after it.
copy.tl: Ang kaligtasan sa laboratoryo ay sumusunod sa tatlong simpleng yugto: maging READY bago ang eksperimento, maging CAREFUL habang ginagawa ito, at mag-CLEAN pagkatapos nito.
copy.bis: Ang kaluwasan sa laboratoryo nagsunod sa tulo ka yano nga yugto: mag-READY sa dili pa ang eksperimento, mag-CAREFUL samtang gihimo kini, ug mag-CLEAN pagkahuman.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: you record the observations and data, then analyze the results, often using graphs to see patterns clearly
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: examine a local weather chart to make simple interpretations about the local weather and describe and practice safety precautions to use during poor or extreme weather conditions
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes general post-experiment data recording and analysis with graphs. It does not mention weather charts, local weather interpretation, or safety precautions for poor/extreme weather, which are the core of G4-E-6.

copy.en: After an experiment, you record the observations and data, then analyze the results, often using graphs to see patterns clearly.
copy.tl: Pagkatapos ng experiment, itinatala mo ang mga observation at data, pagkatapos ay sinusuri ang mga resulta, madalas gamit ang mga graph para makita nang malinaw ang mga pattern.
copy.bis: Pagkahuman sa experiment, imong irekord ang mga observation ug data, dayon analisahon ang mga resulta, kanunay nga mogamit og mga graph aron makita sa klaro ang mga pattern.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Recover means getting useful energy or materials back from waste
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that work is done when a force causes the displacement of an object
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines waste recovery (getting useful energy/materials from waste), which is an environmental/waste-management concept. G8-F-6 requires recognizing that work is done when a force causes displacement of an object, a physics concept. The card provides no information about force, displacement, or work, and is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: Recover means getting useful energy or materials back from waste, so instead of throwing something away, people find a way to use what is still valuable in it.
copy.tl: Ang recover ay nangangahulugang pagkuha muli ng kapaki-pakinabang na enerhiya o materyal mula sa basura, kaya sa halip na itapon ang isang bagay, hinahanapan ito ng paraan upang magamit ang mahalagang bahagi nito.
copy.bis: Ang recover nagpasabot nga makuha pag-usab ang mapuslanong enerhiya o materyal gikan sa basura, busa imbes nga ilabay ang usa ka butang, mangita ug paagi nga magamit ang bililhon nga bahin niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Essential elements like carbon, oxygen, and nitrogen move between living things and the non-living environment
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify examples of how objects can affect other objects even when they are not in contact with each other, such as magnets attracting other objects, light from the sun, and loud noises hurting our ears
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes biogeochemical cycling of elements, not non-contact forces or effects between objects. It does not support the competency about objects affecting other objects without contact (e.g., magnets, light, sound).

copy.en: Essential elements like carbon, oxygen, and nitrogen move between living things and the non-living environment, so the materials of life are recycled again and again.
copy.tl: Ang mahahalagang elemento tulad ng carbon, oxygen, at nitrogen ay umiikot sa pagitan ng mga bagay na may buhay at ng kapaligirang walang buhay, kaya ang mga materyales ng buhay ay paulit-ulit na nire-recycle.
copy.bis: Ang importanteng mga elemento sama sa carbon, oxygen, ug nitrogen nagtuyok tali sa mga butang nga may kinabuhi ug sa kalikopan nga walay kinabuhi, busa ang mga materyales sa kinabuhi gi-recycle balik-balik.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Planting trees and using less fuel from cars and factories can help reduce the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss how bodies of water and landforms affect typhoons
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses reducing atmospheric carbon dioxide, which is unrelated to how bodies of water and landforms affect typhoons.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Planting trees and using less fuel from cars and factories can help reduce the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to explain: a. how typhoons develop, and b. why the Philippines is prone to typhoons
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about carbon dioxide reduction, not about how typhoons develop or why the Philippines is prone to typhoons.

copy.en: Planting trees and using less fuel from cars and factories can help reduce the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere.
copy.tl: Ang pagtatanim ng mga puno at pagbabawas ng paggamit ng gasolina mula sa mga sasakyan at pabrika ay makakatulong na mabawasan ang dami ng carbon dioxide sa atmosphere.
copy.bis: Ang pagtanom ug mga kahoy ug pagpakunhod sa paggamit ug gasolina gikan sa mga sakyanan ug pabrika makatabang nga makunhoran ang gidaghanon sa carbon dioxide sa atmosphere.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: balance reflexes do this faster than you can even think
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes balance reflexes, which are part of the nervous system. G4-L-1 requires describing how the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory systems work. The card does not address any of these five systems, so it does not support the competency.

copy.en:
What keeps you from falling when you slip?

When you suddenly slip or trip, your arms shoot out and your body shifts stance instantly — balance reflexes do this faster than you can even think.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pumipigil sa iyo na madapa kapag nadulas?

Kapag biglang nadulas o natisod ka, kusang umaabot ang iyong braso at nagbabago ang tindig ng katawan mo — ginagawa ito ng balance reflex nang napakabilis, bago ka pa makapag-isip.
copy.bis:
Unsay nagpugong nimo aron dili matumba kung madakin-as?

Kon kalit kang madakin-as o mapandol, motuy-od dayon ang imong bukton ug mausab ang tindog sa lawas — buhaton kini sa balance reflex nga paspas kaayo, sa wala pa ka makahunahuna.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A reflex skips waiting for your brain to decide
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why reflexes are fast, which concerns the nervous system. G4-L-1 requires describing how the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, or respiratory systems work. Reflexes are not part of any of these systems, and the card provides no information about them.

copy.en:
Why is a reflex so fast?

A reflex skips waiting for your brain to decide — that's what makes it faster than a move you choose to make.
copy.tl:
Bakit mabilis ang reflex?

Hindi na naghihintay ng desisyon ng utak ang reflex — kaya mas mabilis ito kaysa sa galaw na sinasadya mong gawin.
copy.bis:
Nganong paspas ang reflex?

Dili na maghulat sa desisyon sa utok ang reflex — mao nga mas paspas kini kaysa sa lihok nga imong tinuyo nga buhaton.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The floating fats in sinigang can be removed by decantation or by scooping them off the top with a spoon
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the differences between animals with a backbone (vertebrates) and animals without backbones (invertebrates) by using common local examples of each group
assignedReviews.reason: Decanting sinigang fat is unrelated to animals with or without a backbone.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The floating fats in sinigang can be removed by decantation or by scooping them off the top with a spoon
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: Decanting sinigang fat is unrelated to using a table to classify living things.

copy.en: The floating fats in sinigang can be removed by decantation or by scooping them off the top with a spoon.
copy.tl: Ang mga lumulutang na taba sa sinigang ay maaaring alisin sa pamamagitan ng decantation o sa pagsandok sa mga ito mula sa itaas gamit ang kutsara.
copy.bis: Ang mga naglutaw nga tambok sa sinigang mahimong makuha pinaagi sa decantation o sa pagsandok kanila sa ibabaw gamit ang kutsara.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: renewable energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe mutations as changes in DNA or chromosomes and discuss some of the factors that cause mutations, such as infectious agents, radiation, and chemicals
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the cost and long-term savings of renewable energy (solar panels). It contains no information about mutations, DNA, chromosomes, or mutagens, which are the subject of G9-L-3.

copy.en: Is renewable energy too expensive for homes?\n\nThe initial installation, like for solar panels, can be costly, but in the long run it reduces your electricity bill by powering your appliances for free.
copy.tl:
Masyado bang mahal ang renewable energy para sa mga bahay?

Ang paunang pag-install, tulad ng solar panels, ay maaaring magastos, pero sa katagalan, binabawasan nito ang iyong electric bill sa pamamagitan ng libreng pagpapaandar ng iyong mga appliances.
copy.bis:
Mahal ba kaayo ang renewable energy para sa mga balay?

Ang unang pag-install, sama sa solar panels, mahimong gasto, apan sa kadugayan, makapakunhod kini sa imong electric bill pinaagi sa libreng pagpadagan sa imong mga appliances.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water is a renewable resource because the water cycle continuously moves it around the Earth
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about the water cycle and water as a renewable resource, which is Earth science content. It provides no information about the respiratory system (nose, windpipe, lungs) or how they work.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water is a renewable resource because the water cycle continuously moves it around the Earth
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about the water cycle and water as a renewable resource, which is Earth science content. It provides no information about the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, or respiratory human body systems.

copy.en: Water is a renewable resource because the water cycle continuously moves it around the Earth, cleaning and refilling our supplies.
copy.tl: Ang tubig ay renewable resource dahil paulit-ulit itong pinapagalaw ng water cycle sa mundo, kaya nalilinis at napupunan muli ang ating mga suplay.
copy.bis: Ang tubig usa ka renewable resource tungod kay ang water cycle padayong nagpalihok niini sa kalibotan, busa mahinlo ug mapuno pag-usab ang atong mga suplay.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Repair is fixing or restoring broken items to be used again
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses repairing broken items for reuse; it contains no information about factors affecting the movement of objects such as size, shape, heaviness, material, or surface texture.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Repair is fixing or restoring broken items to be used again
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: plan and carry out a scientific investigation to determine the effect of different surfaces on the size of frictional forces
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about repair and reuse, not about planning or carrying out an investigation on friction or the effect of different surfaces on frictional forces.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Repair means fixing broken items like a loose chair leg or a torn bag so they can be used again instead of being thrown away.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe conservation of energy in everyday situations involving gravity, such as when objects fall
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines repair of broken items; it contains no information about conservation of energy, gravity, or falling objects. It does not support the competency in any way.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Repair means fixing broken items like a loose chair leg or a torn bag so they can be used again instead of being thrown away.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify examples of everyday situations that demonstrate: a. kinetic energy being transformed to potential energy, and b. potential energy being transformed to kinetic energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses repairing items for reuse; it does not address kinetic or potential energy transformations. It is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: Repair is fixing or restoring broken items to be used again, so defective products should not be immediately thrown away.
copy.tl: Ang Repair ay ang pagkukumpuni o pagpapanumbalik ng mga sirang bagay para magamit muli, kaya ang mga depektibong produkto ay hindi dapat agad itapon.
copy.bis: Ang Repair mao ang pag-ayo o pagpabalik sa mga guba nga butang aron magamit pag-usab, busa ang mga depektibong produkto dili dapat dayon ilabay.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Segmented worms like earthworms and leeches have bodies made of repeated parts
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the purpose of specialized structures in plants, such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, and aerial roots
assignedReviews.reason: The competency G5-L-7 is about specialized structures in plants (rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, aerial roots). The card describes segmented worms (animals) and their repeated body parts, which is unrelated to plant structures. The card does not support the competency in any way.

copy.en: Segmented worms like earthworms and leeches have bodies made of repeated parts, which helps them move easily and flexibly.
copy.tl: Ang mga segmented worm tulad ng earthworm at linta ay may mga katawan na gawa sa paulit-ulit na bahagi, na tumutulong sa kanila na gumalaw nang madali at may flexibility.
copy.bis: Ang mga segmented worm sama sa earthworm ug linta adunay mga lawas nga gihimo sa gibalikbalik nga mga parte, nga makatabang kanila sa paglihok nga sayon ug flexible.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Clear procedures allow others to replicate your investigation
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe a valence electron as an electron in the outer shell of an atom that can take part in formation of bonds
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why clear procedures enable replication of an investigation. It contains no information about valence electrons, atomic structure, or chemical bonding, which are the subject of G9-M-3.

copy.en:
Why must your procedures be clear enough for someone else to follow?

Clear procedures allow others to replicate your investigation, which means they can repeat it exactly to check if they get the same results!
copy.tl:
Bakit kailangang malinaw ang iyong procedures para masundan ng iba?

Ang malinaw na procedures ay nagbibigay-daan sa iba na i-replicate ang iyong investigation, ibig sabihin maaari nilang ulitin ito nang eksakto para tingnan kung pareho ang makukuhang resulta!
copy.bis:
Ngano kinahanglan nga klaro ang imong procedures aron masunod sa uban?

Ang klaro nga procedures nagtugot sa uban nga i-replicate ang imong investigation, nagpasabot nga mahimo nila kining usbon sa eksakto aron tan-awon kung pareho ba ang ilang makuha nga resulta!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Friction is the resistance to motion of one object moving relative to another object it touches.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines friction, a physics concept, and has no relation to the respiratory system (nose, windpipe, lungs) required by G5-L-2. This is a living-things tag applied to a physics card.

copy.en: Friction is the resistance to motion of one object moving relative to another object it touches.
copy.tl: Ang friction ay ang resistance sa motion ng isang bagay na gumagalaw kaugnay sa isa pang bagay na nakadikit dito.
copy.bis: Ang friction mao ang resistance sa motion sa usa ka butang nga naglihok kalabot sa laing butang nga gihikap niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The health of an estuary can be repaired by re-establishing freshwater inflow
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses estuary health and freshwater/saltwater balance, with no mention of plant outer parts (leaves, roots, stems) or their roles in water/nutrient uptake. It does not support the G3-L-5 competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The health of an estuary can be repaired by re-establishing freshwater inflow
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in a guided investigation to identify the effect of different types of soil on the growth of plants
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about restoring freshwater inflow to an estuary, not about investigating the effect of different soil types on plant growth. No soil or plant growth content is present, so it does not support G4-E-3.

copy.en: The health of an estuary can be repaired by re-establishing freshwater inflow, which brings back the right balance of fresh and salt water.
copy.tl: Ang kalusugan ng isang estuary ay maaaring maayos sa pamamagitan ng pagpapanumbalik ng freshwater inflow, na nagbabalik ng tamang balanse ng freshwater at saltwater.
copy.bis: Ang kahimsog sa usa ka estuary mahimong ayohon pinaagi sa pagpabalik sa freshwater inflow, nga magabalik sa husto nga balanse sa freshwater ug saltwater.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Reuse them for water on hot days!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about reusing fizzy drink bottles for water, which is unrelated to the competency on investigating reflection and refraction of light using mirrors, lenses, and prisms.

copy.en:
What can you do with fizzy drink bottles instead of throwing them away?

Reuse them for water on hot days!
copy.tl:
Ano ang maaari mong gawin sa mga fizzy drink bottles sa halip na itapon ang mga ito?

I-reuse ang mga ito para sa tubig sa mainit na mga araw!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang mahimo nimo sa mga fizzy drink bottles imbes nga ilabay kini?

I-reuse kini alang sa tubig sa init nga mga adlaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Clean and tidy papers can be cut and used as notebook covers or for arts and crafts.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: differentiate plant and animal cells based on their organelles
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes reusing paper for notebook covers or arts and crafts, which is unrelated to differentiating plant and animal cells based on organelles.

copy.en: Clean and tidy papers can be cut and used as notebook covers or for arts and crafts.
copy.tl: Ang malinis at maayos na mga papel ay maaaring gupitin at gamitin bilang pabalat ng notebook o para sa arts and crafts.
copy.bis: Ang limpyo ug hapsay nga mga papel mahimong guntingon ug gamiton isip hapin sa notebook o para sa arts and crafts.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Reverse faults are associated with convergent boundaries, where tectonic plates push together and compress the crust.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss the factors that limit the ecosystem's carrying capacity, such as adequate food, shelter, water, and mates
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes reverse faults and convergent plate boundaries, which is geology/earth science content. G10-L-10 concerns factors limiting an ecosystem's carrying capacity (food, shelter, water, mates). There is no connection to living things or ecosystems.

copy.en: Reverse faults are associated with convergent boundaries, where tectonic plates push together and compress the crust.
copy.tl: Ang mga reverse fault ay nauugnay sa convergent boundaries, kung saan nagsasalpukan ang mga tectonic plate at pinipiga ang crust.
copy.bis: Ang mga reverse fault nalangkit sa convergent boundaries, diin ang mga tectonic plate magbangga ug mopislit sa crust.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Rheology is the study of how Earth's materials flow and deform
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate and describe the relationship among the projectile variables including the angle and velocity of release, and projectile height and range, using everyday activities such as shooting basketballs or kicking footballs
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains rheology of Earth's layers and lithosphere-asthenosphere movement, which is unrelated to projectile motion variables (angle, velocity, height, range). No instructional support for G10-F-1.

copy.en: Rheology is the study of how Earth's materials flow and deform, and it helps explain how the rigid lithosphere moves over the flowing asthenosphere.
copy.tl: Ang rheology ay ang pag-aaral kung paano dumadaloy at nagde-deform ang mga material ng Earth, at nakakatulong itong ipaliwanag kung paano gumagalaw ang matigas na lithosphere sa dumadaloy na asthenosphere.
copy.bis: Ang rheology mao ang pagtuon kon giunsa pagdagayday ug pag-deform ang mga material sa Earth, ug makatabang kini pagpasabot kon giunsa paglihok sa gahi nga lithosphere sa nagdagayday nga asthenosphere.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A rice cooker saves time in cooking
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a rice cooker saving time by automatically cooking and keeping rice warm. This has no relation to describing air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor. The assigned competency is about the composition of air, which is not addressed or supported by the card content.

copy.en: A rice cooker saves time in cooking because it automatically cooks rice and keeps it warm until you are ready to eat.
copy.tl: Ang rice cooker ay nakakatipid ng oras sa pagluluto dahil kusa itong nagsasaing at pinananatiling mainit ang kanin hanggang handa ka nang kumain.
copy.bis: Ang rice cooker makadaginot ug oras sa pagluto kay kini awtomatikong magluto ug bugas ug magpainit sa kan-on hangtod andam ka nang mokaon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A rice field is a man-made wetland where farmers grow rice in standing water, and it becomes a home for frogs, snails, and wading birds!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate proper use and handling of science equipment
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a rice field as a habitat for living things. It contains no content about science equipment, its proper use, or handling, which is the subject of G7-M-12.

copy.en:
What makes a rice field a special habitat?

A rice field is a man-made wetland where farmers grow rice in standing water, and it becomes a home for frogs, snails, and wading birds!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nagpapaspesyal sa palayan bilang habitat?

Ang palayan ay gawa ng tao na wetland kung saan nagtatanim ng palay ang mga magsasaka sa nakatayong tubig, at nagiging tahanan ito ng mga palaka, kuhol, at mga ibong tumatawid sa tubig!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang nagpaspecial sa basakan isip habitat?

Ang basakan kay hinimo sa tao nga wetland diin ang mga mag-uuma nagtanom og humay sa nagbarog nga tubig, ug kini nahimong pinuy-anan sa mga baki, kuhol, ug mga langgam nga molatas sa tubig!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Ridge push is a force that moves plates when new seafloor forms at a mid-ocean ridge
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate and explain the observable effects of predictable patterns and events including changes in seasons, changes observed in the patterns of visible star over a year, and solar and lunar eclipses
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes ridge push, a plate tectonics mechanism. G6-E-8 concerns the Sun-Earth-Moon system model, seasons, star patterns, and eclipses. No instructional support for that competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Ridge push is a force that moves plates when new seafloor forms at a mid-ocean ridge
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate the rotation of the Earth on its axis using a globe to explain day and night
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about plate movement via ridge push, not about Earth's rotation on its axis or day and night. It does not support G6-E-7.

copy.en: Ridge push is a force that moves plates when new seafloor forms at a mid-ocean ridge and pushes the older, cooler seafloor away from the ridge.
copy.tl: Ang ridge push ay puwersa na nagpapagalaw sa mga plate kapag nabubuo ang bagong seafloor sa mid-ocean ridge at tinutulak nito ang mas lumang seafloor palayo sa ridge.
copy.bis: Ang ridge push usa ka puwersa nga nagpalihok sa mga plate kon maporma ang bag-ong seafloor sa mid-ocean ridge ug gitulak ang mas daan nga seafloor palayo sa ridge.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Ring of Fire is a geographic area around the Pacific Ocean where many active volcanoes are found along plate boundaries.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some examples of longitudinal waves, and transverse waves
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the Ring of Fire and volcanic activity along plate boundaries; it provides no information about longitudinal or transverse waves, so it does not support identifying examples of these waves.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Ring of Fire is a geographic area around the Pacific Ocean where many active volcanoes are found along plate boundaries.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify differences and similarities between longitudinal waves and transverse waves
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about volcanoes and plate boundaries, not wave types; it gives no content on differences or similarities between longitudinal and transverse waves.

copy.en: The Ring of Fire is a geographic area around the Pacific Ocean where many active volcanoes are found along plate boundaries.
copy.tl: Ang Ring of Fire ay isang geographic area sa paligid ng Pacific Ocean kung saan maraming aktibong bulkan ang matatagpuan sa mga plate boundary.
copy.bis: Ang Ring of Fire usa ka geographic area libot sa Pacific Ocean diin daghang aktibo nga mga bulkan ang makita sa mga plate boundary.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Two river communities can act like a fair test
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in the weather can affect daily activities and explain how some types of weather can be dangerous for people
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about a fair test comparing clean and polluted rivers, not about weather changes affecting daily activities or dangerous weather. No support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Two river communities can act like a fair test
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: examine a local weather chart to make simple interpretations about the local weather and describe and practice safety precautions to use during poor or extreme weather conditions
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses pollution and fair test design, not examining a local weather chart, interpreting weather, or safety precautions for poor weather. No support for the competency.

copy.en: Two river communities can act like a fair test, where the clean river is the control group and the polluted river is the experimental group, with pollution as the one changed factor.
copy.tl: Ang dalawang komunidad sa tabing-ilog ay maaaring kumilos tulad ng isang fair test, kung saan ang malinis na ilog ay ang control group at ang maruming ilog ay ang experimental group, na ang polusyon ang isang binagong factor.
copy.bis: Ang duha ka komunidad sa daplin sa suba mahimong molihok sama sa usa ka fair test, diin ang limpyo nga suba mao ang control group ug ang hugaw nga suba mao ang experimental group, nga ang polusyon mao ang usa ka giusab nga factor.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Meiosis is important for sexual reproduction because it produces gametes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe different science process skills used in performing simple science activities, such as observing, predicting, and measuring using units such as millimeter, centimeter, and meter
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the role of meiosis in sexual reproduction and fertilization, which is a biology topic. G3-M-4 is about describing science process skills (observing, predicting, measuring) in simple activities. There is no connection to science process skills or measurement units.

copy.en: Meiosis is important for sexual reproduction because it produces gametes, and fertilization restores the diploid chromosome number in the zygote.
copy.tl: Mahalaga ang meiosis para sa sexual reproduction dahil gumagawa ito ng gametes, at ibinabalik ng fertilization ang diploid chromosome number sa zygote.
copy.bis: Importante ang meiosis alang sa sexual reproduction tungod kay mopatungha kini og gametes, ug ibalik sa fertilization ang diploid chromosome number sa zygote.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You can roll an empty can across a table using only a charged balloon
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a labelled diagram to describe the connections between the levels of biological organization to one another from cells to the biosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a static electricity demonstration (charged balloon moving a can), which is a physics concept. G7-L-8 is about levels of biological organization from cells to biosphere, a biology topic. No biological organization content is present.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You can roll an empty can across a table using only a charged balloon
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about static charge and motion, not about body systems working together. G8-L-2 requires models/flow charts/diagrams to explain how body systems cooperate (e.g., digestion and excretion). The card has no biology content.

copy.en: You can roll an empty can across a table using only a charged balloon, because the balloon's charge pulls on the can's charges without touching it.
copy.tl: Maaari mong pagulungin ang isang empty can sa mesa gamit lamang ang charged balloon, dahil hinihila ng charge ng balloon ang mga charge sa lata nang hindi ito hinahawakan.
copy.bis: Mahimo nimo nga paligiron ang walay sulod nga lata sa lamesa gamit lamang ang charged balloon, tungod kay ang charge sa balloon mobira sa mga charge sa lata nga wala kini hikapa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A rose plant can reproduce a whole new plant if a piece of its stem is placed into water or soil, a type of vegetative reproduction.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: express quantitatively the amount of solute present in a given volume of solvent
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about vegetative reproduction in plants; it provides no information about expressing the amount of solute in a given volume of solvent.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A rose plant can reproduce a whole new plant if a piece of its stem is placed into water or soil, a type of vegetative reproduction.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of pure substances as: a. having fixed chemical composition, examples of which are elements and compounds, and b. that all the atoms of an element have a unique number of protons
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about plant reproduction, not about pure substances, fixed chemical composition, elements, compounds, or unique proton numbers.

copy.en: A rose plant can reproduce a whole new plant if a piece of its stem is placed into water or soil, a type of vegetative reproduction.
copy.tl: Ang halamang rosas ay kayang magparami ng buong bagong halaman kung ang isang piraso ng stem nito ay ilalagay sa tubig o lupa, isang uri ng vegetative reproduction.
copy.bis: Ang tanom nga rosas makapasanay ug tibuok bag-ong tanom kon ang usa ka piraso sa stem niini ibutang sa tubig o yuta, usa ka klase sa vegetative reproduction.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Displacement only cares about where you start and where you end
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to explain how lines of evidence, such as fossils, biogeography, and comparative morphology, support the occurrence of evolution
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches displacement in a round trip (physics), which is unrelated to using secondary sources to explain how fossils, biogeography, and comparative morphology support evolution.

copy.en:
If I walk to school and then walk back home, what is my total displacement?

Zero! Displacement only cares about where you start and where you end, and since you end at home, your starting and ending positions are the same.
copy.tl:
Kung maglakad ako papuntang school at bumalik sa bahay, ano ang total displacement ko?

Zero! Ang displacement ay tumitingin lang sa kung saan ka nagsimula at kung saan ka natapos, at dahil natapos ka sa bahay, pareho ang starting at ending position mo.
copy.bis:
Kung molakaw ko paingon sa school ug mobalik sa balay, unsa ang akong total displacement?

Zero! Ang displacement nagtan-aw lang kung asa ka nagsugod ug asa ka nahuman, ug tungod kay nahuman ka sa balay, pareho ang imong starting ug ending position.
